title: Charges dropped against 16-year-old arrested in connection with fatal Pensacola shooting - NewsBreak
text:
By Hannah O’Gara ,
2 hours ago
PENSACOLA, Fla. (WKRG) — The State Attorney’s Office confirms charges have been dropped against a 16-year-old who was charged with aggravated assault and unlawful possession of a firearm by a minor in connection with the deadly Downtown Pensacola Fourth of July shooting.
How Daphne firefighters protect community through extreme summer heat wave Court records show the minor’s case is now closed. The 16-year-old was arrested on July 13th.
Pensacola Police originally said he handed a gun to one of the other suspects, 26-year-old Nicolas Safford, who’s charged with aggravated assault, possession and firing of a weapon.
The State Attorney’s Office told News 5 that charges for the minor were dropped due to no probable cause.
Alongside Safford, 25-year-old Lillian Meyers is charged with obstructing justice, and a 17-year-old is charged with possession and firing of a weapon.
On July 16, Pensacola Police tried to arrest 20-year-old Trevon Bradley for manslaughter. But police confirmed when they arrived at his apartment complex, Bradley shot and killed himself.
Bradley was suspected of killing 19-year-old Phillip “PJ” Sheppard during a shootout in downtown Pensacola during the early morning hours of July 5th.
Daphne police search for stabbing suspect, victim recovering in ICU Upon news that the 16-year-old’s charges were dropped, Pensacola Mayor D.C. Reeves took to social media saying:
“We bring full closure to this case. All four suspects involved have been accounted for and located. Though one suspect tragically took his own life, the relentless pursuit of justice by our officers ensures our community can now rest easier.”
